title: On the Concept of Arithmetic Conseqeunce
summary: Gödel's second incompleteness theorem is standardly understood as showing that no sufficiently strong, consistent theory of arithmetic can prove its own consistency, a result typically interpreted against a model-theoretic background in which arithmetical language is evaluated with respect to an independently given structure of natural numbers. This paper develops an alternative perspective grounded in proof-theoretic semantics.
